title: Why Do Onions Make You Cry?
pause_note: 'long' lists beat indices followed by a pause; Short: 0.6 s

beats: Why does cutting an onion make you cry?
A whole onion doesn't. Only a cut one.
Inside each cell, the onion keeps two things apart: a harmless sulfur compound, and an enzyme.
Your knife breaks the cells, and the two mix.
A second enzyme turns the result into a stinging gas.
It drifts up and reaches the nerves on the surface of your eye.
Your eye does the only thing it can: it makes tears to wash it away.
Chill the onion first, and the enzymes work more slowly.
Scientists have even made onions with almost none of that second enzyme. They hardly make you cry.
The onion isn't sad. It's a chemical trap, and your knife springs it.
